overview.description: King Pedro is a variant of the popular American card game Pedro (also known as Cinch or 63), played primarily in the northeastern United States and Canada. It adds the King of trumps as an additional scoring card worth 5 points, making the total points available 19 per hand instead of the standard 14. It is a trick-taking game where the 5 of trumps (the Pedro) and the 5 of the same color (the Left Pedro) are the most valuable cards.

history.origins: Developed from the 19th-century American game Pedro (also called Cinch or Double Pedro). The addition of the King as a scoring card was a regional variation that emerged in the northeastern United States and parts of Canada.
timeline: Mid-1800s: Original Pedro game develops from Pitch in the United States
Late 1800s: Pedro becomes extremely popular across the US
Early 1900s: Regional variants like King Pedro emerge in the Northeast
Present: Still played in parts of Canada and the northeastern US
history.evolution: King Pedro represents one of several 'augmented' Pedro variants where additional scoring cards were added. Other variants include Sixty-three (63) and Eighty-three (83), which add even more scoring cards.
history.cultural: Pedro and its variants were extremely popular in the US at the end of the 19th century. While its popularity declined in the 20th century, it remains beloved in specific regions including southern Louisiana, parts of Canada, and the northeastern US.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other.
setup.dealing: Deal 9 cards to each player, 3 at a time. The turn to deal passes to the left after each hand.

rules.objective: Be the first team to reach 62 or more points by winning tricks containing valuable cards.
rules.gameplay: The high bidder leads to the first trick. If a trump is led, players must play a trump if possible. If a non-trump is led, players must follow suit or trump if possible. Highest trump wins the trick; if no trumps, highest card of led suit wins. Winner leads to next trick.
keyRules: Deal 9 cards each (3 at a time); dealer rotates left. One round of bidding from dealer's left; minimum bid 7, maximum 14; must bid higher or pass; dealer forced to bid 7 if all pass. High bidder names trumps; everyone discards all non-trumps face down; dealer replenishes others to 6 cards and takes remainder (all trumps) for own hand. High bidder leads; follow suit or trump when possible; highest trump wins trick, else highest of led suit; winner leads next. First team to 62 or more points wins; bidder goes out rule when both teams 55+.

strategy.basic: The Pedro (5 of trumps) and Low Pedro (other 5 of same color) are worth 10 points togetherâ€”more than half the available points. Prioritize capturing or protecting these cards.
strategy.intermediate: When bidding, consider not just your trumps but whether you have protection in side suits. A hand with the two Pedros and a few other trumps is strong even without the Ace or King.
strategy.advanced: The King of trumps adds 5 points, making it as valuable as a Pedro. If you hold the King and several other trumps, you have a strong hand for bidding. Watch for situations where you can force opponents to play their Pedros by leading high trumps.
tips: If you have more than 6 trumps after the discard, you must play multiple cards to the first trick (burying the extras)
The Low Pedro can be a surpriseâ€”remember which suit is the same color as trump
In close games, remember the 'bidder goes out' rule: if both teams are near 62, the bidding team wins if they make their bid
Don't forget the trump Twoâ€”it scores 1 point for the team that was dealt it

difficulty.medium: Recognizes the value of holding both Pedros; reasonable bidding; tracks played trumps
difficulty.hard: Optimal bidding based on complete hand evaluation; perfect tracking of all scoring cards; calculates probabilities of opponents holding Pedros

play_card.description: Play one card to the current trick. If trump is led, play a trump if possible; if non-trump is led, follow suit or trump if possible. Highest trump wins the trick; if no trumps, highest card of led suit wins. Winner leads to the next trick.
play_card.constraints: Must follow suit when possible; if trump led must play trump if able; only one card per trick except when burying extra trumps on the first trick.

draw.reason: This game has no draw-from-stock action.

discard.description: Discard all non-trump cards face down after the high bidder names trumps. Dealer then replenishes other players to six cards and takes the remainder (all trumps) for own hand.
discard.constraints: After trump is declared; discard only non-trumps; illegal to discard scoring trumps; players with more than six trumps keep them and will play multiple cards to the first trick.

pass.constraints: During bidding only; one chance per player; once you pass you are out of the auction for that hand.

bid.description: Bid a number (points your team will take if you choose trumps). Minimum 7, maximum 14. Each bid must be higher than the previous bid. Dealer is forced to bid 7 if the first three players pass.
bid.constraints: During bidding phase only; one round starting to dealer's left; must bid higher than previous bid or pass.

meld.reason: This game has no meld action.

go_out.reason: This game has no go-out action.

edgeCases.text: Bidder goes out: when both teams have 55 or more, the next hand is bidder-goes-out; bidding team wins the game if they make their bid.
If both teams reach 62+ in the same hand when it was not bidder-goes-out, play one more bidder-goes-out hand to decide the winner.
A player with more than six trumps after replenishment must play multiple cards to the first trick (bury extras); illegal to bury any scoring trump.
Dealer must take all trumps from the remaining deck and may have more than six cards; dealer replenishes others to six before taking from remainder.
Trump two (low) scores 1 point for the team that was dealt it, not for the team that wins the trick.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.
